First, we note that 

$$
F(t)=\int {F}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t=\int ⟨\frac{16\sqrt[3]{t}}{3},\,5{e}^{5t}⟩\text{d}t.
$$

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨\frac{16\sqrt[3]{t}}{3},\,5{e}^{5t}⟩\,\text{d}t & =⟨\int \frac{16\sqrt[3]{t}}{3}\,\text{d}t,\int 5{e}^{5t}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{4/3}+{c}_{1},\,{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The initial condition $F(0)=⟨2,\,-1⟩$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}F(0)=⟨4\cdot {0}^{4/3}+{c}_{1},\,{e}^{5\cdot 0}+{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨2,\,-1⟩ \\ ⟨{c}_{1},\,1+{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨2,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${c}_{1}=2$ and ${c}_{2}=-2.$ Consequently

$$
F(t)=⟨4{t}^{4/3}+2,\,{e}^{5t}-2⟩.
$$
